name: Jāmiʿ al-bayān
author: Muḥammad ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī
about: The earliest complete tafsir to survive: every reading reported of the ayah, with its chain, and then his judgement between them.

name: Maʿālim al-tanzīl
author: al-Ḥusayn al-Baghawī
about: A tafsir by transmission of moderate length, valued for its care with the reports and its plain style.

name: al-Jāmiʿ li-aḥkām al-Qurʾān
nameEnglish: The Compendium of the Qurʾan’s Rulings
author: Shams al-Dīn al-Qurṭubī
about: Built around the rulings drawn from each ayah, question by question, with the language and the reports behind them.

name: Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿaẓīm
author: Ismāʿīl ibn Kathīr
about: The Qurʾan explained by the Qurʾan, then by hadith, then by the early generations. The full Arabic, not the abridgement.

name: al-Nukat wa-l-ʿuyūn
author: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Māwardī
authorArabic: أبو الحسن علي بن محمد الماوردي
about: Numbers the opinions held on each phrase and names who held them, adding his own reasoning where they differ.

name: Zād al-masīr
author: Abū al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzī
about: Sets the differing views on each phrase side by side, briefly, and names who held each.

name: Tafsīr Ibn al-Qayyim
nameEnglish: The Tafsir of Ibn al-Qayyim, collected
author: Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyya
about: What he wrote on the ayat, gathered from across his books. It covers about a third of them.

name: Baḥr al-ʿulūm
author: Abū al-Layth al-Samarqandī
authorArabic: أبو الليث نصر بن محمد السمرقندي
about: An early Ḥanafī tafsir from Samarqand: short explanations, most of them reported from the Companions and their students.

name: al-Kashf wa-l-bayān
author: Abū Isḥāq al-Thaʿlabī
authorArabic: أبو إسحاق أحمد بن محمد الثعلبي
about: A large tafsir from Nishapur gathering a great many reports and stories, not all of them sound; al-Baghawī's Maʿālim al-tanzīl abridges it and leaves the weak ones out.

name: al-Hidāya ilā bulūgh al-nihāya
author: Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib
about: A full tafsir by the Andalusian master of the readings: the meaning, the readings, the grammar and what is abrogated, ayah by ayah.

name: Tafsīr al-Qurʾān
author: Abū al-Muẓaffar al-Samʿānī
authorArabic: أبو المظفر منصور بن محمد السمعاني
about: A tafsir of moderate length by a Shāfiʿī scholar of hadith, careful to keep to the reports and to the creed of the early generations.

name: al-Tashīl li-ʿulūm al-tanzīl
author: Ibn Juzayy al-Kalbī
authorArabic: محمد بن أحمد بن جزي الكلبي
about: A compact Andalusian tafsir — the meaning, the language and the rulings in short notes — opening with a valued introduction to the sciences of the Qurʾan.

name: al-Jawāhir al-ḥisān
author: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Thaʿālibī
about: An Algerian scholar's tafsir that abridges Ibn ʿAṭiyya's al-Muḥarrar al-wajīz, with additions of his own.

name: Fatḥ al-qadīr
author: Muḥammad al-Shawkānī
about: Joins the two methods — what is narrated and what is reasoned — in one work of moderate length.

name: Fatḥ al-bayān
author: Ṣiddīq Ḥasan Khān al-Qinnawjī
about: A commentary by the Indian scholar of Bhopal, drawing closely on al-Shawkānī's Fatḥ al-qadīr.

name: Maḥāsin al-taʾwīl
author: Jamāl al-Dīn al-Qāsimī
about: A late commentary by a scholar of Damascus that quotes the earlier masters at length on each passage — Ibn Taymiyya and Ibn al-Qayyim above all.

name: Mafātīḥ al-ghayb
author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
about: A vast, argued commentary — theology, language and law — taken one question at a time.

name: Rūḥ al-maʿānī
author: Maḥmūd Shihāb al-Dīn al-Ālūsī
about: A vast commentary from Baghdad gathering the earlier works — language, rhetoric, theology and the readings — and closing many passages with the 'indications' the Sufis drew from them.

name: Naẓm al-durar
titleArabic: نظم الدرر في تناسب الآيات والسور
author: Burhān al-Dīn al-Biqāʿī
authorArabic: برهان الدين إبراهيم بن عمر البقاعي
about: Explains how each ayah follows from the one before it, and each surah from the last: the coherence of the Qurʾan's order.

name: Aḍwāʾ al-bayān
author: Muḥammad al-Amīn al-Shinqīṭī
about: Explains ayat by other ayat, with long treatments of the rulings. It covers about a third of the ayat.

name: al-Tafsīr al-basīṭ
author: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Wāḥidī
authorArabic: أبو الحسن علي بن أحمد الواحدي
about: The longest of al-Wāḥidī's three tafsirs, given above all to the language: the grammar, the meanings of words and the poetry that attests them.

name: al-Muḥarrar al-wajīz
titleArabic: المحرر الوجيز في تفسير الكتاب العزيز
author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya al-Andalusī
authorArabic: عبد الحق بن غالب بن عطية الأندلسي
about: The Andalusian tafsir that weighs the reports and the language with great care; al-Qurṭubī and Abū Ḥayyān both lean on it.

name: al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ
author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Andalusī
authorArabic: أبو حيان محمد بن يوسف الأندلسي
about: The grammarian's tafsir: the grammar, the forms and the readings of every phrase set out at length, and the meaning after.

name: Irshād al-ʿaql al-salīm
titleArabic: إرشاد العقل السليم إلى مزايا الكتاب الكريم
author: Abū al-Suʿūd al-ʿImādī
authorArabic: أبو السعود محمد بن محمد العمادي
about: The Ottoman chief mufti's tafsir: concise, and given to the Qurʾan's eloquence and the reasons behind its wording.

name: al-Taḥrīr wa-l-tanwīr
author: Muḥammad al-Ṭāhir ibn ʿĀshūr
about: The fullest modern work on the Qurʾan’s language, its rhetoric and how each passage is put together.

name: Tafsīr Ibn ʿUthaymīn
author: Muḥammad ibn Ṣāliḥ al-ʿUthaymīn
about: His lessons, transcribed: the explanation, then the benefits drawn from each ayah. It covers about half the ayat.

name: Aysar al-tafāsīr
author: Abū Bakr al-Jazāʾirī
about: Plain lessons on each passage for the general reader: its words explained, its meaning, and the guidance to take from it.

name: al-Mukhtaṣar fī al-tafsīr
author: Markaz Tafsīr
credit: Markaz Tafsīr, a committee of scholars
about: A plain paragraph on what the ayah says, written by a committee of scholars. The place to start.

name: al-Qurʾān: tadabbur wa-ʿamal
author: Sharikat al-Khibrāt al-Dhakiyya
about: Short reflections on each page of the muṣḥaf, and what a reader can do with them.

name: Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿazīz
author: Ibn Abī Zamanīn
authorArabic: محمد بن عبد الله بن أبي زمنين
about: An Andalusian Mālikī's abridgement of the early tafsir of Yaḥyā ibn Sallām, keeping to the reports of the first generations.

name: al-Wajīz
author: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Wāḥidī
authorArabic: أبو الحسن علي بن أحمد الواحدي
about: The shortest of al-Wāḥidī's three tafsirs: the meaning of each ayah in a line or two.

name: Anwār al-tanzīl
author: Nāṣir al-Dīn al-Bayḍāwī
about: A dense, compact commentary on the language and the meaning; a standard teaching text for centuries.

name: Madārik al-tanzīl
author: Abū al-Barakāt al-Nasafī
authorArabic: أبو البركات عبد الله بن أحمد النسفي
about: A Ḥanafī teaching text in the manner of al-Bayḍāwī: brief, exact notes on the language and the meaning.

name: Tafsīr al-Jalālayn
nameEnglish: The Commentary of the Two Jalāls
author: Jalāl al-Dīn al-Maḥallī and Jalāl al-Dīn al-Suyūṭī
authorArabic: جلال الدين المحلي وجلال الدين السيوطي
about: The ayah glossed phrase by phrase. The most widely taught short tafsir there is.

name: Jāmiʿ al-bayān
author: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ījī
about: A concise commentary in short phrases, glossing the meaning of each ayah.

name: Tafsīr Qatāda
author: Qatāda ibn Diʿāma al-Sadūsī
about: What Qatāda, of the generation after the Companions, said on the ayat, gathered from the books that report him.

name: Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿaẓīm musnadan
nameEnglish: Commentary on the Mighty Qurʾan, with its chains
author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
authorArabic: عبد الرحمن بن أبي حاتم الرازي
about: The reports and nothing else — from the Prophet ﷺ, the Companions and their students — each with its chain. Parts of it are lost, so it does not cover every ayah.

name: al-Durr al-manthūr
author: Jalāl al-Dīn al-Suyūṭī
about: The reports and nothing else: what was narrated on each ayah from the Prophet ﷺ, the Companions and their students.

name: Maʿānī al-Qurʾān
author: Abū Zakariyyā al-Farrāʾ
authorArabic: أبو زكريا يحيى بن زياد الفراء
about: The great grammarian of Kufa on the language of the Qurʾan: how its phrases are built, its readings and its idiom.

name: Majāz al-Qurʾān
author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar ibn al-Muthannā
about: One of the first books on the Qurʾan's language: how its expressions run in the speech of the Arabs, shown from their poetry.

name: Tafsīr gharīb al-Qurʾān
nameEnglish: The Rare Words of the Qurʾan Explained
author: Ibn Qutayba al-Dīnawarī
authorArabic: عبد الله بن مسلم بن قتيبة الدينوري
about: One of the earliest books on the Qurʾan's unfamiliar words, by the great man of letters of Baghdad.

name: Maʿānī al-Qurʾān wa-iʿrābuh
nameEnglish: The Meanings of the Qurʾan and its Grammar
author: Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj
authorArabic: أبو إسحاق إبراهيم بن السري الزجاج
about: A grammarian of Baghdad on the meanings of the Qurʾan: how each phrase is construed, and what follows from that for its sense.

name: Maʿānī al-Qurʾān
author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
authorArabic: أبو جعفر أحمد بن محمد النحاس
about: The meanings of the Qurʾan's words and phrases, with the views of the early grammarians and commentators set against each other. It survives only in part.

name: al-Tibyān fī tafsīr gharīb al-Qurʾān
nameEnglish: The Exposition of the Qurʾan's Rare Words
author: Ibn al-Hāʾim
authorArabic: شهاب الدين أحمد بن محمد ابن الهائم
about: A short handbook of the Qurʾan's unfamiliar words, in the order of the muṣḥaf.

name: al-Sirāj fī bayān gharīb al-Qurʾān
nameEnglish: The Lamp, on the Qurʾan's Rare Words
author: Muḥammad al-Khuḍayrī
about: The unfamiliar words of each ayah, each explained in a few words: a modern handbook to keep beside the muṣḥaf.

name: al-Muyassar fī gharīb al-Qurʾān
nameEnglish: The Rare Words of the Qurʾan, Simplified
author: King Fahd Complex
authorArabic: مركز الدراسات القرآنية بمجمع الملك فهد
credit: The Centre for Qurʾanic Studies, King Fahd Complex
about: The unfamiliar words of each ayah, briefly explained, from the Qurʾanic studies centre of the King Fahd Complex.

name: Asbāb nuzūl al-Qurʾān
author: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Wāḥidī
authorArabic: أبو الحسن علي بن أحمد الواحدي
about: The reports of what occasioned particular ayat, with their chains: the best-known book of its kind. Not every report in it is sound.

name: Aḥkām al-Qurʾān
author: Abū Bakr al-Jaṣṣāṣ
authorArabic: أبو بكر أحمد بن علي الجصاص
about: The ayat that carry rulings, read by a leading Ḥanafī jurist of Baghdad, with the arguments between the schools.

name: al-Īḍāḥ li-nāsikh al-Qurʾān wa-mansūkhih
nameEnglish: The Clarification of What Abrogates and What Is Abrogated
author: Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib
about: Makkī on the ayat said to abrogate or to be abrogated: what is claimed of each, and which claims hold.

name: Aḥkām al-Qurʾān
author: Ilkiyā al-Harrāsī
about: The ayat of rulings from the Shāfiʿī side, by a student of al-Juwaynī.

name: Aḥkām al-Qurʾān
author: Abū Bakr ibn al-ʿArabī
authorArabic: أبو بكر محمد بن عبد الله ابن العربي
about: The Mālikī judge of Seville on the ayat that carry rulings, question by question.

name: al-Iklīl fī istinbāṭ al-tanzīl
nameEnglish: The Crown, on Drawing Rulings from the Revelation
author: Jalāl al-Dīn al-Suyūṭī
about: Al-Suyūṭī's short book of the rulings and lessons that have been drawn from the ayat.

name: Aḥkām al-Qurʾān
author: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Ṭarayfī
about: A contemporary study of the ayat of rulings, drawing on how the first generations understood them. It covers part of the Qurʾan.
